notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) via background subagents covering 2026-10-15/16. Routine EGRESS_BLOCKED/DNS-failure on nearly every org-domain WebFetch; all four lanes worked around it via WebSearch, same pattern as prior runs. The two same-day announcement items that actually landed in the window were TSMC's record Q3 2026 earnings (Oct 15) and a federal CISA deadline to patch an actively-exploited Ivanti Connect Secure flaw that lands today (Oct 16) -- otherwise this was a forward-looking-calendar run: AI model retirement/deprecation dates pulled from Anthropic's and OpenAI's own deprecation pages (OpenAI legacy-model shutdown Oct 23, OpenAI image-API retirement Dec 1, OpenAI fine-tuning job-creation cutoff Jan 6 2027, Azure's GPT-5 retirement Feb 5 2027, Claude Sonnet 4.5's Nov 30 API retirement), a cluster of devtools/cloud EOL and conference dates (Kubernetes 1.34 EOL, Node.js 26 Active LTS, AWS Lambda Python 3.10 end of patches, Amazon Pinpoint end of support, GitHub Enterprise Server 3.19 EOL, AWS re:Invent, Microsoft Ignite, Google Cloud Next 2027, KubeCon EU 2027), and a certificate/crypto-policy cluster in security (Let's Encrypt's 64-day default validity, CA/Browser Forum's 100-day ballot, Mozilla's 2008-2009-era root distrust, plus two deadlines computed from explicit day-count rules stated in OMB's and CISA's own primary documents: OMB M-26-15's 120-day post-quantum migration-plan deadline and CISA BOD 26-04's 180-day compliance deadline). Earnings-calendar items without an official company press release (Alphabet, Qualcomm, Nvidia Q3/Q4 estimates) and a rumored, unconfirmed Apple October 27 event were deliberately left out as too weakly sourced for this calendar; a routine monthly GitLab point release was also left out as too low-value to be worth an engineer's attention. The run landed at the 40-entry cap after that trimming.
concerns: The bigtech/hardware/mobile lane re-found Google's official Play Console policy table listing the geofencing/Contacts/Location/SMS permission changes at 2027-01-27 -- but data/events/2027-01.json already carries three near-duplicate entries for this same policy change at this same date (a standing issue flagged in multiple prior runs' concerns, caused by a title-token-overlap gap in src/lib/id.ts). Deliberately not filed a fourth time this run; a maintainer should merge the existing cluster before any future lane re-adds it.

The FTC v. Amazon antitrust trial date remains unsettled: one source (court order) says February 9, 2027, while a separate joint proposal from both parties seeks to push it to late March 2027 with no confirmation found that a judge has granted it. Filed at 'expected' confidence with the court-ordered date, flagged here since it may move again before the window closes in on it.

OMB's post-quantum migration-plan deadline (2026-10-22) and CISA BOD 26-04's full-compliance deadline (2026-12-07) are not written out as calendar dates on any primary page found this run -- they are this run's own arithmetic applied to an explicit day-count rule stated in the primary documents themselves (120 days from M-26-15's June 24, 2026 issuance; 180 days from BOD 26-04's June 10, 2026 effective date). The arithmetic was double-checked and both dates are correct, but a maintainer with direct access to OMB's and CISA's own compliance trackers should confirm neither agency has since published a different operative date.

Microsoft's fiscal Q1 2027 earnings date (Oct 28) and Apple's fiscal Q4 2026 earnings date (Nov 2) were re-confirmed this run from independent secondary sources quoting each company's own press release -- both should already match what prior runs filed, so this is intended as a corroborating correction, not a new fact.

AWS's own Lambda runtimes page explicitly flags its Node.js 26 / Python 3.15 runtime-addition date (Nov 2026) and Aurora PostgreSQL 16.8/17.4 end-of-standard-support date (Nov 2026) as indicative and subject to change -- filed at month precision and 'expected' confidence rather than a specific day, per the no-guessing-dates rule.
